dataset: Full Court Buckets WNBA team revenue and franchise value multiples
revenue_definition: 2025 team revenue estimates in millions of U.S. dollars. The column 2025_revenue_usd_m is the Playbook Strategies figure used for the FCB multiple. Playoffs are excluded, as labeled on the Oct. 31, 2026 Playbook graphic and in the Forbes methodology. These are estimates, not audited financials.
valuation_definition: Forbes franchise value in millions of U.S. dollars from the May 7, 2026 ranking of the 13 teams that played in 2025. Forbes includes arena economics and excludes arena real estate. Values were read from the Forbes Mexico translation of the Brett Knight article, which prints the 13 team cards. The English Forbes URL is the canonical citation.
multiple_definition: value_to_revenue_multiple is a Full Court Buckets calculation: forbes_2026_value_usd_m divided by 2025_revenue_usd_m (the Playbook estimate), rounded half up to one decimal. It is not a multiple Forbes published team by team, except that Forbes stated Golden State at about 10 times 2025 revenue and the league at 12.5 times average 2025 regular-season revenue.
timing_note: Revenue is for the 2025 season. Forbes values are as of the May 7, 2026 ranking. This page was updated Oct. 31, 2026, during the 2026 WNBA Finals. The 2026 season's revenue is not in these figures.

sources.title: The WNBA's Most Valuable Teams 2026
sources.author: Brett Knight
sources.notes: Canonical citation. On Oct. 31, 2026 the English page returned a JavaScript shell to a non-JS client, so the 13 team cards were not in that response. Search text of the article still states Golden State at $780 million and $78 million of revenue, a combined $5.4 billion, and a $414 million average. A public snippet also shows an Aug. 18, 2026 update line. This file does not assume that update changed any team card.

sources.title: Estos son los equipos mas valiosos de la WNBA en 2026
sources.author: Brett Knight
sources.role: Translation of the Forbes US article, with the 13 team cards
sources.notes: The page says the text was first published in Forbes US. Cards, in rank order: value, one-year change, 2025 revenue, and the owner line Forbes printed. Revenue methodology on the same page: 2025 estimates rounded to the nearest million, playoffs excluded, arena economics included, arena real estate excluded. Portland Fire and Toronto Tempo omitted. Golden State was not given a one-year change.

sources.title: WNBA Market Intelligence 2026
sources.author: Katherine Rowe
sources.role: 2025 revenue estimates used for the FCB multiple
sources.notes: The Oct. 31, 2026 graphic on Katherine Rowe's post is the revenue column for this dataset. The graphic credits Forbes for 2026 values (May 7, 2026) and says the 2025 revenue estimates exclude playoffs. The report page asks for a name and email before the PDF. FCB used the public graphic, not an unlocked PDF.

sources.title: WNBA Franchise Valuations 2026 Disagree by $220M
sources.author: Tyler Maldonado
sources.role: Secondary republication of a Forbes-style table
sources.notes: The table matches the Forbes Mexico cards on value, one-year change, and Forbes revenue, including a complete Atlanta row at $250 million and $16 million. It conflicts with Playbook on Indiana ($58 million vs $56 million) and Washington ($18 million vs $16 million). It does not conflict with the Forbes prose that names those revenue figures.

sources.title: WNBA Team Values 2026: Valkyries Lead at $850M, Average Jumps 59%
sources.role: Different valuation model. Not used in the FCB value column.
sources.notes: Sportico values Golden State at $850 million, the Liberty at $600 million, the Fever at $560 million, and the Storm at $425 million. The 13 teams that played in 2025 are $5.55 billion combined, average $427 million, including real estate and practice facilities. Sportico also wrote that those 13 teams generated an estimated $410 million in revenue, that Golden State generated $78 million, and that Atlanta generated a league-low $16 million. The Fever value and the league revenue total do not match Forbes or Playbook. A line that Golden State's $78 million was 48 percent more than the Fever does not reconcile to either $56 million or $58 million, so FCB does not derive a Fever revenue from it.

sources.title: WNBA team valuations: Valkyries, Liberty, Fever lead most valuable women's basketball franchises in 2026
sources.role: Secondary table that matches Sportico's scale, not Forbes
sources.notes: Prints Golden State at $850 million and an average of $427 million, up 59 percent. The Dream is last at $280 million in that table, not the Forbes $250 million. Toronto Tempo and Portland Fire are described as excluded. FCB does not use this table for values.

sources.title: CNBC's Official WNBA Team Valuations 2026
sources.role: Different model and a 15-team set. Not used in the FCB value column.
sources.notes: CNBC values Golden State at $1 billion and puts the average of 15 franchises at $460 million. That set includes teams that had not played in 2025. FCB does not use these values.

sources.title: Indiana Fever named third most valuable WNBA franchise by Forbes
sources.role: Rejected. The table does not match Forbes May 7, 2026.
sources.notes: The story attributes a table to Forbes that lists Golden State at $1 billion and includes the Portland Fire and Toronto Tempo. Those values are not the May 7, 2026 Forbes cards. The same story also says the Fever generated over $58 million and that the Liberty and Aces generated $43 million and $34 million, which does match Forbes revenue prose, and that the average value is $414 million. FCB uses none of the FOX59 team values.

sources.title: The WNBA's Most Valuable Teams 2026
sources.role: Audio read of the Forbes article
sources.notes: The transcript repeats the Forbes prose: Fever $58 million, Liberty $43 million, Aces $34 million, no team worth less than $250 million, and an average of $414 million, up 52 percent from $272 million.

arena_note: Arena names are the strings on WNBA.com team pages when FCB checked team facts on Oct. 28, 2026. They are context, not an input to the Forbes value.
rejected_note: Future expansion clubs in Cleveland, Detroit, and Philadelphia are also outside the Forbes May 7, 2026 ranking. Forbes said they begin play in 2028, 2029, and 2030. They are not given rows here.
